user.title: Govee API key
user.description:
Enter your Govee Developer API key from {api_url}.

This is not your Govee account password. It is a separate developer key.

data_description.api_key: The API key from your Govee Developer account (a long string of letters and numbers).

account.title: Govee account (optional)
account.description:
For real-time updates, enter your Govee mobile app credentials below.

**Important:** Use the email and password from the Govee mobile app. The app password may differ from the Govee website password.

To skip this step, leave both fields empty and submit.

data_description.email: The email address you use to sign in to the Govee mobile app.
data_description.password: The password you use to sign in to the Govee mobile app (not the website).

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Govee
reauth_confirm.description: Your API key is no longer valid. Enter a new one.

data_description.api_key: A current API key from the Govee Developer account this integration was set up with.

verification_code.title: Govee verification code
verification_code.description: A verification code has been sent to **{email}**. Enter the code below. The code expires in approximately 15 minutes.

data_description.verification_code: Check your email for a code from Govee.

data_description.api_key: Your Govee Developer API key from developer.govee.com.
data_description.email: Email for the Govee mobile app. Leave empty to remove real-time updates.
data_description.password: Password for the Govee mobile app. Leave empty to keep the existing password.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Govee device found nearby
bluetooth_confirm.description: {name} was found over Bluetooth. Govee devices are controlled through your Govee cloud account, so the next step asks for your Govee API key.

error.invalid_auth: Invalid API key. Check that you are using the developer key from developer.govee.com, not your account password.
error.invalid_account: Invalid Govee app credentials. Make sure you are using the password from the Govee mobile app (not the website).
error.invalid_api_key_format: The API key looks invalid. It should be a long string (36 or more characters) from developer.govee.com.
error.password_without_email: Enter both email and password, or leave both empty to skip.
error.email_without_password: Enter both email and password, or leave both empty to skip.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the Govee API. Check your internet connection.
error.invalid_verification_code: Invalid or expired verification code. Check your email and try again.
error.login_rejected: Govee rejected the login request. This may be a temporary server issue; try again later.

abort.already_configured: This Govee API key is already configured
abort.missing_credentials: The account email and password were not provided
abort.already_in_progress: A Govee set-up is already in progress.

general.title: Govee options
general.description: If you have RGBIC devices, per-device segment settings will appear after submitting.

data.enable_mqtt_control: Send power, brightness, and color over MQTT (faster, experimental)
data.confirm_commands: Confirm light commands and resend dropped ones
data.enable_lan_nudge: Re-check device state locally after cloud updates
data.enable_lan_raw_write: Send segment colours over the local network
data.enable_zone_lights: Split a multi-zone lamp into per-zone lights

data_description.poll_interval: How often every device is polled over the Govee cloud API for its state. Real-time updates over MQTT and LAN arrive between polls. Range 30 to 300 seconds, default 60. Each poll spends one request per device against Govee's limit of 100 per minute and 10,000 per day.
data_description.daily_request_budget: How many Govee cloud requests per day this integration aims to spend on polling. The polling interval is stretched automatically so the day's spend lands on this figure. Govee's own cap is 10,000 per day; the default of 9,000 leaves headroom for commands, scene lookups and device rediscovery.
data_description.api_temperature_unit: Auto (default) first uses the temperature unit your Govee account reports for the device, then falls back to converting the thermometers known to report Fahrenheit (for example H5179, H5109, H5110, H5111, H5053, H5075, H5100), and trusts the rest. Choose Fahrenheit if a reading still looks about 1.8 times too high (for example 74 instead of 23), or Celsius to force no conversion. Govee's API omits unit metadata, so the value cannot always be auto-detected.
data_description.water_detector_poll_interval: How often standalone Govee water and leak detectors (for example H5054) are checked for a leak. These RF-only sensors have no push channel, so a leak surfaces with up to this much delay. Lower reacts faster but makes more account API calls; raise it if you have many detectors. Range 60 to 3600 seconds, default 120. Requires email and password login; ignored if you have no such detectors.
data_description.probe_poll_interval: How often an armed probe (cooking) thermometer such as the H5192 is read over AWS IoT while its Live polling switch is on. These devices never volunteer a reading, so this interval is the update rate. Costs battery rather than API quota. Range 10 to 600 seconds, default 30. Requires email and password login.
data_description.mqtt_status_interval: How often every MQTT-connected device is asked for its current status over AWS IoT. Devices are largely poll-triggered responders, not autonomous pushers; this mirrors what the Govee app itself does while its device list is on screen, so state keeps updating without the app open. Lower reacts faster but publishes more per device; raise it if you have many devices. Range 60 to 3600 seconds, default 300. Set 0 to turn the re-query off and rely on what devices push on their own. Queries go out one device per second; a device whose query makes AWS IoT close the session twice is left out until the next reload (a warning names it). If the session closes right after queries to three different models in a row with none answered, AWS IoT is refusing status queries for the whole account, and the re-query stops until the next reload (a warning says so). Requires email and password login (MQTT credentials); ignored when MQTT is unavailable.
data_description.enable_groups: Surfaces the device groups you created in the Govee app as single light entities. A command to a group is sent once and synced to all members by Govee's cloud, so it syncs better than grouping the lights with Home Assistant helpers. State is best-effort (groups cannot be polled), and group lights only support power, brightness, and color.
data_description.enable_scenes: Creates a scene dropdown per device that has scenes, and exposes the scenes as light effects. Turn off to save one API request per device at startup.
data_description.enable_diy_scenes: Creates a DIY scene dropdown per device that has DIY scenes created in the Govee app.
data_description.expose_transport_entities: Adds one connectivity binary sensor per transport (cloud API, MQTT, Bluetooth, LAN) for every device. Off by default because it creates four extra diagnostic entities per device.
data_description.enable_mqtt_control: Routes power, brightness, and color commands through Govee's MQTT channel instead of the REST cloud API, reducing latency and bypassing REST rate limits. Requires email and password login (MQTT credentials). Falls back to REST automatically when MQTT is unavailable, and for any device that has not yet answered over MQTT (it answers the periodic status query, so keep that on). Experimental: it uses an undocumented channel, so leave it off if commands behave unexpectedly.
data_description.confirm_commands: After a power-off, brightness, colour or colour-temperature command to a light, waits a few seconds for the light's own real-time (AWS IoT) report and asks for one status if none comes. If the light still shows the old value, the command is sent once more over the cloud API. Lights only: appliances such as kettles, heaters and fans are never resent, and a power-on is never resent. A resend uses one cloud request, only when the daily budget and rate limit allow it. Requires email and password login; lights that have not reported over AWS IoT are left as they are. Off by default.
data_description.lan_targets: Only needed when LAN-enabled Govee devices are on a different subnet or VLAN than Home Assistant, so the local discovery scan cannot reach them. Enter a comma-separated list of device IPs (10.20.0.51), broadcast addresses (10.20.0.255), and subnets in CIDR notation (10.20.0.0/24, /24 or smaller). Subnets are scanned device by device, since most routers drop cross-VLAN broadcasts. Leave blank if all devices share Home Assistant's network. Advanced: if a device still is not found because its scan reply cannot cross the VLAN, pin it with device_id=ip (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11=10.20.0.51) to skip discovery for that device. Add a trailing ! (=10.20.0.51!) only for firmware that accepts LAN commands but never answers a status read. That turns off every LAN health check for the device, so a wrong IP will look like it is working while the device never responds. Enter off to turn LAN discovery and local control off entirely.
data_description.enable_lan_nudge: When the cloud reports a change made outside Home Assistant, the device's real state is read over the local network instead of trusting the push. Locally discovered devices only.
data_description.enable_lan_raw_write: Segment colour and brightness act immediately instead of taking Govee's cloud round trip. Works on locally discovered lamps with a supported model; others keep using the cloud. Segment state can't be read back, so entities show the last command sent. Zone lights do not need this option — they always use the local network.
data_description.enable_ble_raw_write: For lamps with no local Wi-Fi control. Needs a Bluetooth adapter or an active Bluetooth proxy in range. While a command is being sent, the Govee phone app may briefly be unable to connect.
data_description.enable_zone_lights: Each zone becomes its own light and the lamp's own entity becomes a dimmable master. Automations that set an effect on the lamp entity must target a zone or the scene selector instead. Zone state shows the last command sent — the device cannot report it back.
data_description.enable_h6104_ble: Use experimental Bluetooth control and status readback for H6104 TV lights. Requires a connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy.

kettle_slots.title: Kettle slot labels: {device_name}
kettle_slots.description: Optional display labels for the kettle's custom slots, for example the names you gave them in the Govee app. The mode itself stays Custom 1-4 (custom_1-custom_4 in automations); the labels appear in the entities' labels attribute. Leave a field blank for no label. A label may not repeat another label, a built-in mode, Manual or Off.

select_segment_devices.title: Select segment devices
select_segment_devices.description: Choose which RGBIC devices to configure segment modes for.

data_description.devices: Devices to set a segment mode for. Devices you leave out keep their current mode.

configure_device_mode.title: Segment mode: {device_name}
configure_device_mode.description: Choose how segments are created for **{device_name}** (`{device_id}`).

data_description.segment_mode: Disabled creates no segment entities, grouped creates one entity for all segments, individual creates one entity per segment, both creates the grouped entity alongside the individual ones, and custom groups creates one entity per group you define below.
data_description.segment_groups: Name each group and list its segments, separated by semicolons - e.g. "Left: 1-5; Right: 6-10". Ranges and comma lists both work. Groups may not overlap.
data_description.segment_count: How many segments the device really has. Pre-filled with the cloud's count, which can be wrong for models the integration has not measured.

error.invalid_lan_targets: One of the LAN device addresses is not a valid IP, broadcast address, subnet (/24 or smaller), or device_id=ip override. Example: 10.20.0.51, 10.20.0.255, 10.20.0.0/24, AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11=10.20.0.51
error.unknown_lan_device: A device_id=ip override names a device that is not on this Govee account. Copy the device ID exactly as it appears in the device's diagnostics (for example AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11).
error.segment_groups_zero_groups: Define at least one segment group.
error.segment_groups_invalid_syntax: Each group must be "Name: indices", separated by semicolons - e.g. "Left: 1-5; Right: 6-10".
error.segment_groups_empty_group: Every group needs at least one segment.
error.segment_groups_too_large: A group can have at most 16 segments.
error.segment_groups_out_of_range: One of the segment numbers is outside this device's segment count.
error.segment_groups_overlap: Groups cannot share the same segment.
error.duplicate_slot_label: Two slots have the same label.
error.reserved_slot_label: This label is a built-in mode, Manual or Off.

abort.kettle_unavailable: The kettle is no longer available. Open the options again.

options.groups: Custom groups (one entity per group you define)

refresh_scenes.name: Refresh scenes
refresh_scenes.description: Refreshes the available scenes from the Govee API.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device to refresh. Leave empty to refresh every device. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

set_segment_color.name: Set segment color
set_segment_color.description: Sets the color of specific segments on an RGBIC light.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The RGBIC light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

segments.name: Segments
segments.description: List of segment indices, starting at 0.

rgb_color.name: RGB color
rgb_color.description: Color as [R, G, B] values from 0 to 255.

send_raw_ptreal.name: Send raw ptReal frame
send_raw_ptreal.description: Developer/debug tool that sends raw Govee BLE command frames to the device, over the local network when its LAN connection is healthy and over AWS IoT otherwise (a checksum is added automatically when 19 bytes or fewer are given). Several comma-separated frames go out together in one message, the way the Govee app uploads a scene. A wrong frame can leave the light in an unexpected mode.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device to send the frame to. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

frame.name: Frame
frame.description: The raw BLE command frame as hex bytes, separated by spaces or colons (e.g. "33 05 15 01 FF 00 00"). Up to 20 bytes; a checksum is appended automatically for 19 bytes or fewer. Separate several frames with commas to send them in one message.

upload_bulb_positions.name: Upload bulb positions
upload_bulb_positions.description: Stores a 3D position map on a string light, one [x, y, z] point per bulb in LED order, with y as height. The light draws its position-aware effects from this map. Replaces the map the light holds. Takes about 14 seconds for 300 bulbs.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The string light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

positions.name: Positions
positions.description: A list of [x, y, z] points, one per bulb, in LED order. The list must cover every bulb.

normalize.name: Normalize
normalize.description: Scale the points uniformly into a 0-500 cube with the minimum at the origin, keeping the shape's proportions, as the Govee app does. Turn off to send integer coordinates (0-1000) unchanged.

apply_diy_effect.name: Apply DIY effect
apply_diy_effect.description: Composes and uploads a DIY effect to one lamp. Target exactly one device. On a multi-zone lamp, fill the zone fields: a zone with every field empty (or mode "none") is switched off, and an omitted field uses its fixed default, not the currently staged value. On a string light, fill the whole-light fields or give 1 to 3 layers. Zone lamps require the per-zone lights option.

ripple_mode.name: Ripple mode
ripple_mode.description: Effect mode for the ripple zone. Pick a name, or enter a number 0-255. "none" - or leaving every ripple field empty - switches the zone off.

ripple_speed.name: Ripple speed
ripple_speed.description: Transition speed for the ripple zone. Default 50.

ripple_colors.name: Ripple colors
ripple_colors.description: Palette for the ripple zone as a list of [R, G, B] triplets, in the order the effect cycles them (1-16 colors). Required whenever the zone is used with a mode other than "none".

ripple_direction.name: Ripple direction
ripple_direction.description: Motion of the ripple effect: cw, ccw, or reverse (a back-and-forth sweep).

ripple_flow_rate.name: Ripple flow rate
ripple_flow_rate.description: Water flow rate for the ripple zone. Default 50.

ring_mode.name: Ring mode
ring_mode.description: Effect mode for the ring zone. Pick a name or type a raw number 0-255. "none" (or omitting every ring field) switches the zone off.

ring_speed.name: Ring speed
ring_speed.description: Transition speed for the ring zone. Default 50.

ring_colors.name: Ring colors
ring_colors.description: Palette for the ring zone as a list of [R, G, B] triplets, in the order the effect cycles them (1-16 colors). Required whenever the zone is used with a mode other than "none".

effect.name: Effect
effect.description: Whole-light effect type, for string lights. The numbered names, mountain_peak, candy_crush, smudge, whirlpool and flexing follow the composer tiles of the Govee app. "combo" plays the effects named in Combine.

colors.name: Colours
colors.description: The palette: a list of up to 8 colours, each [red, green, blue]. Most effects need at least two. Fade, breathe, combo, ribbon, mountain_peak, candy_crush, smudge, flexing, spiral, starlight and wave take one; spin_3 needs three; bounce, whirlpool, diffuse_1 and diffuse_2 need four.

speed.name: Speed
speed.description: 0 to 100 (1 to 100 for combo). Leave empty for the effect's stock speed.

direction.name: Direction
direction.description: Leave empty for the effect's stock direction. Flow 1, rainbow 1 and spin 1-2 take clockwise or anticlockwise. Flow 2-4 take up, down, clockwise, anticlockwise, upper left, expand vertically or gather vertically. Stripes take up, down, clockwise, anticlockwise and the four diagonals; rainbow 2 takes the four diagonals. Smudge and blend take up or down, whirlpool takes gather or expand horizontally, and spiral takes the four upward and downward turns. Flow, layered, rainbow, vortex and rotate take any direction; every other effect takes none.

combine.name: Combine
combine.description: For the combo effect only: 1 to 4 of flow_1, rainbow_1, fade_1, marquee_3 and breathe, each once. They share the colours and speed.

shape.name: Shape
shape.description: For the flexing effect only: round, square or rhomb. Leave empty for rhomb.

center.name: Centre point
center.description: For the flexing effect only: the point the shape grows from. Leave empty for center.

params.name: Parameter block
params.description: The bytes between the effect id and the colour count, as a list of numbers 0 to 255. Replaces the effect's own block, for example with a stock scene's block. It must have the length of the effect's own block, and wave, ribbon, mountain_peak, flexing and candy_crush must keep its first byte. Speed, direction, shape and centre are written over it when given. Every other byte is sent unchecked. Not for the older-format effects or combo.

layers.name: Layers
layers.description: Stacks 1 to 3 effects into one, for string lights. Each layer is an object with effect, colors and optional speed, direction, shape, center and params, checked as the fields above check one effect. Layers are sent in the order given. The older-format effects (flow_1, rainbow_1, fade, marquee, breathe) and combo cannot be layers. Leave the fields above empty when giving layers.

layer_mode.name: Layer mode
layer_mode.description: The two header bytes of a layered effect: default (2, 0), variant_3 (3, 0) or variant_1_2 (1, 2). Stock scenes use all three. Leave empty for default. Only with layers.

request_status.name: Request status
request_status.description: Asks a device to report its status over AWS IoT (the real-time connection), once or repeatedly for a while. Needs the account login. Spends no cloud API requests.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The device to ask. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Keep asking for this many seconds (up to 120). 0 asks once.

interval.name: Interval
interval.description: Seconds between queries while repeating (at least 3).

set_light_timer.name: Set light timer
set_light_timer.description: Sets one of the light's on-device on/off timers over the local raw-frame connection. The light keeps running the timer without Home Assistant.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

slot.name: Timer
slot.description: Which timer to set, counting from 1.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether the timer runs. An enabled timer needs a time and an action. Disabling a timer keeps the time, action and days it has unless you give new ones.

action.name: Action
action.description: What the timer does at its time.

time.name: Time
time.description: Time of day the timer fires.

weekdays.name: Repeat on
weekdays.description: Days to repeat on. Leave empty to run once.

set_sleep_timer.name: Set sleep timer
set_sleep_timer.description: Sets the light's on-device sleep timer over the local raw-frame connection. The light dims from the start brightness to off over the given minutes.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How long the light takes to dim to off.

start_brightness.name: Start brightness
start_brightness.description: Brightness the dimming starts from, in percent.

set_wake_up.name: Set wake-up
set_wake_up.description: Sets the light's on-device wake-up over the local raw-frame connection. The light brightens over the duration so it reaches the end brightness at the time.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether the wake-up runs. An enabled wake-up needs a time.

time.name: Time
time.description: Time of day the light reaches the end brightness.

weekdays.name: Repeat on
weekdays.description: Days to repeat on. Leave empty to run once.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Minutes the light takes to brighten.

end_brightness.name: End brightness
end_brightness.description: Brightness reached at the time, in percent.

color_temp_kelvin.name: Color temperature
color_temp_kelvin.description: White the light wakes up in, in kelvin, within the light's range.

set_music_mode.name: Set music mode
set_music_mode.description: Starts one of the light's on-device music effects over the local raw-frame connection. Effects that take a palette always upload one, the given palette or the default rainbow.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The light. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

manual_color.name: Manual color
manual_color.description: One fixed color instead of the automatic colors. Not every light takes one.

palette.name: Palette
palette.description: Colors for effects that take a palette, as a list of [R, G, B] triplets (1-8 colors). Rhythm takes none.

paint_bulbs.name: Paint bulbs
paint_bulbs.description: Colours individual LEDs of a string light. Named LEDs take their colour and every other LED shows the base colour. The paint replaces whatever the light was showing.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The string light to paint. Accepts a Home Assistant device or a Govee device ID.

colors.name: Colours
colors.description: A list of entries, each with rgb_color ([red, green, blue]) and bulbs. Bulbs are 0-based numbers or ranges written as "first-last". A bulb named twice takes the later colour.

base_color.name: Base colour
base_color.description: Colour of every LED not named. Black leaves them dark.

command_failed.message: Govee did not accept the command for {device}. Check the device's connectivity and the API rate limit, then try again.

device_offline.message: Govee reports {device} as offline, so it did not receive the command. Check that the device has power and a Wi-Fi connection, then try again.

segment_out_of_range.message: Segment indices {indices} are out of range for {device}, which has {count} segments.

not_loaded.message: The Govee integration is not loaded.

invalid_scene_palette.message: {value} is not a scene palette. Give 1 to {maximum} colors as #rrggbb, separated by commas.

scene_setting_unavailable.message: The scene running on {device} has no such setting, or no scene from the catalogue is running.

unsupported_target_humidity.message: {device} does not support a target humidity.

invalid_ptreal_frame.message: {frame} is not a valid raw ptReal frame. Provide 1-20 hex bytes, optionally separated by spaces or colons, with a valid checksum if 20 bytes are given.

ptreal_unavailable.message: Could not send the raw ptReal frame to {device}. This requires a healthy LAN connection to the device or the account (email/password) login with AWS IoT connected, and the device must not be a group.

bulb_positions_unsupported.message: {device} does not take a bulb position map.

bulb_position_count.message: {count} positions were given, but {device} has {expected} bulbs. Give one position per bulb.

invalid_bulb_positions.message: The bulb positions are not valid: {reason}.

bulb_positions_failed.message: Could not finish uploading the position map to {device}: {sent} of {total} packets were sent. This needs a raw-frame option (local raw writes or AWS IoT raw writes) and a reachable device. Upload the whole map again.

bulb_paint_incomplete.message: Could not finish painting {device}: {sent} of {total} packets were sent. Paint it again.

too_many_ptreal_frames.message: {count} frames were given, but at most {max} can be sent in one message.

segment_passthrough_failed.message: Segment 4 of {device} can only be set over the AWS IoT passthrough, which is not connected or did not accept the command. Check the Govee account login and MQTT connection, then try again. Other requested segments may already have changed.

kettle_manual_no_target.message: {device} has no target temperature yet, so Manual cannot be selected.

kettle_target_with_mode.message: Setting a target temperature puts {device} in Manual, so it cannot be combined with the {mode} mode.

status_query_unavailable.message: Cannot ask {device} for its status: this needs the account (email/password) login with AWS IoT connected, and the device must have a topic, not be a group, a model left out of status queries or quarantined, and AWS IoT must not be refusing status queries for the account.

status_query_throttled.message: {device} was asked for its status less than {seconds} seconds ago. Wait a moment and try again.

h6104_bluetooth_required.message: H6104 TV mode requires Bluetooth. Check the Bluetooth adapter or proxy and the Govee diagnostics, then try again.

invalid_tv_sensitivity.message: TV sensitivity must be a whole number from 0 to 100.

raw_action_unavailable.message: Could not send {action} to {device}. This needs a raw-frame option (local raw writes, BLE raw writes or AWS IoT raw writes) and a reachable device.

timer_slot_unknown.message: Timer {slot} on {device} is not known yet, so disabling it needs a time. Give a time, or ask the device for its status first.

timer_needs_time_and_action.message: An enabled timer needs a time and an action.

wake_up_needs_time.message: An enabled wake-up needs a time.

kelvin_out_of_range.message: {kelvin} K is outside the {minimum}-{maximum} K range of {device}.

music_effect_unsupported.message: {effect} is not a music effect of {device}. Its effects are {effects}.

music_manual_color_unsupported.message: {device} takes no manual color in music mode.

music_palette_unsupported.message: The {effect} music effect takes no palette.

music_palette_too_long.message: A music palette takes at most {maximum} colors.

bulb_paint_unsupported.message: {device} does not support painting individual bulbs

invalid_string_effect_layer.message: Cannot apply layer {layer} of the effect to {device}: {reason}

invalid_layer_count.message: A layered effect on {device} takes {min} to {max} layers, not {count}.

layer_mode_without_layers.message: Cannot apply the effect to {device}. Layer mode needs layers.

layers_with_effect_fields.message: Cannot apply the effect to {device}. Leave {fields} empty when giving layers.

confirm.title: Raise the polling interval
confirm.description: The Govee API has rate limited requests for {entry_title}; normal operation resumes in approximately {reset_time}. The polling interval is {current} seconds. Submitting sets it to {proposed} seconds and reloads the integration so it stays inside Govee's request budget. You can change it again later under Configure.

abort.entry_not_found: The Govee entry no longer exists.

confirm.title: Retry the Govee account connection
confirm.description: Real-time updates for {entry_title} are unavailable ({reason}); everything keeps working over polling. Submitting clears the stored sign-in failure and reloads the integration so it signs in and reconnects to Govee's real-time channel. If the account now needs email verification or a new password, a separate repair will ask you to reconfigure.

abort.entry_not_found: The Govee entry no longer exists.

mqtt_silent.title: Govee real-time updates are silent for {entry_title}
mqtt_silent.description:
The real-time (AWS IoT) session for {entry_title} is connected, but in {minutes} minutes not one message arrived, although new readings from your devices reached Govee's cloud or the integration asked them for their status. Reconnecting once did not help. Everything keeps working over polling.

This usually means the saved account sign-in no longer gets updates. Go to the integration page and select **Reconfigure** to sign in again, which fetches fresh real-time credentials. This repair clears itself as soon as a real-time message arrives.

mqtt_2fa_required.title: Govee account requires verification
mqtt_2fa_required.description:
Your Govee account now requires email verification (2FA) to enable real-time MQTT updates for {entry_title}. Go to the integration page and select **Reconfigure** to re-enter your credentials with a verification code.

The integration will continue to work using polling until this is resolved.

mqtt_token_expired.title: Govee account sign-in expired
mqtt_token_expired.description:
The saved Govee account sign-in for {entry_title} has expired, and signing in again was rejected, usually because the account password changed.

While it is expired, battery levels and readings for sensors that reach Govee through a gateway (for example an H5310 or H5112 behind an H5044) stop updating. Lights and everything using the API key are unaffected.

Go to the integration page and select **Reconfigure** to enter the current account password.
